newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb says its Monsanto pact unaffected by deal.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb says its Monsanto pact unaffected by deal.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Monday Monsanto Co's pending acquisition of Holden's Foundation Seeds Inc and its affiliates will have no impact on DeKalb's long-term research collaboration or cross-licensing agreements with Monsanto.

"Assuming that the Holden's transaction is completed, we would not expect it to have any impact on the research projects that we are now pursuing or plan to pursue with Monsanto," Bruce Bickner, DeKalb's chairman, said in a statement.
"Likewise, such acquisition will not affect the cross-licensing agreements between DeKalb and Monsanto relating to corn herbicide or insect resistance," Bickner said.
He added that Monsanto's acquisition of Holden's could, in fact, enhance DeKalb's opportunities for additional royalty income.
Bickner also said the transaction will have no impact on DeKalb's germplasm, since it never transferred rights to its germplasm to Monsanto.
"Furthermore, this acquisition will have no impact on our freedom to commercialize biotechnology products," he said.

In January 1996, DeKalb and Monsanto entered into a biotechnology research collaboration and signed three cross-licensing agreements covering technology relating to insect-resistant and herbicide-resistant corn.
Monsanto also made an equity investment in DeKalb last year, acquiring 10 percent of the class A voting stock and 45 percent of the publicly traded class B non-voting stock.
